_provenance.notes: Alaska sport fishing is a $2.5 billion annual industry — the second most important fisheries sector after commercial. The Kenai River is the economic center of Alaska sport fishing: 16 million angler-days statewide means 100,000+ visitors per year coming specifically for salmon fishing. License sales peaked in 1990 at 618,000 and have generally declined as non-resident fees increased. The dipnetting fishery on the Kenai and Kasilof rivers is a unique Alaskan institution — 52,000 Alaska residents wading in with dip nets to harvest sockeye for personal use, up to 25 fish per household member.

dipnet_fishery.notes: The dipnet fishery is one of Alaska's most beloved summer traditions. During the July window, beaches at the Kenai River mouth are lined with Alaska residents in waders catching sockeye. The scene is unlike anything else in US fisheries management — residents with long-handled dip nets wading in a major river to catch salmon for their freezers.
